title: I Built an Agent That Plays Slay the Spire 2 (15x Faster Than Claude)
description:
I built an agent that plays Slay the Spire 2, and it decides every move in about 315 milliseconds for $0.00046. That is 15x faster and 259x cheaper than Claude scoring the exact same decisions.

The code is public and so are the numbers. Run the benchmark yourself and tell me I'm wrong:
https://github.com/shoemoney/jev-the-spire2

WHAT IT USES
TypeSafe Jev is a decision model, not a chat model. You hand it a state and typed questions, it returns calibrated probabilities, and it never generates text. No prompt begging for JSON, no regex stripping code fences off the answer.

The trick is that it evaluates every question in one request in parallel. I measured 160 questions answering as fast as 31. So a decision that needs many judgments costs ONE round trip, not many, and the multi-call pipeline I started with was the entire latency problem.

THE HEAD TO HEAD (same 10 fixtures, byte-identical state, 30 decisions each)
  Kimi K3            29/30    2,312ms    $0.01111
  Claude Opus 5.5    29/30    3,590ms    $0.04704
  Claude Fable 5.1   29/30    5,534ms    $0.11952
  Grok 4.7           29/30   12,022ms    $0.01303
  TypeSafe Jev       27/30      315ms    $0.00046
  GPT-6 Astra        24/30    1,672ms    $0.03210
  DeepSeek 4.1 Flash 24/30   23,366ms    $0.00446

Being straight with you: 27 vs 29 is inside the noise floor on a 10-fixture corpus, so Jev is NOT smarter than Claude here. What IS real is 6x to 63x on speed and 24x to 260x on cost. Opus 5.5 is the best LLM on that board and it isn't close.

THREE THINGS THAT COST ME REAL TIME
1. A scoring factor that didn't separate the candidates still voted at full strength, because min-max normalising a 0.01 spread stretches it to a full swing. Adding a deadband was worth +16 points on its own.
2. Capping the question fan-out to "save money" silently switched the reasoning off on the most crowded boards. It killed a run at 7 HP.
3. The API's latency is bimodal, fast or 40x slower with nothing in between, so waiting longer never helps but firing a second request does.
